desc:
A lock has four wheels, each showing a digit from 0 to 9. A combination is written as an integer from 0 to 9999 whose four digits are the wheels, with leading zeros understood: 7 means wheels 0-0-0-7 and 120 means 0-1-2-0. The lock starts at combination 0 (0-0-0-0).

One move turns a single wheel one step up or one step down, and wheels wrap around: one step up from 9 gives 0 and one step down from 0 gives 9.

The combinations in deadends jam the lock. As soon as the wheels show one of them, the lock is stuck, so a dead-end combination can never be passed through. Return the minimum number of moves needed to reach target, or -1 if it is impossible. (If the starting combination 0 itself is a dead end, or the target is, the answer is -1.)

deadends = [2],             target = 3        -> 5   (0000, 0010, 0011, 0012, 0013, 0003)
deadends = [],              target = 5555     -> 20
deadends = [1,9,10,90,100,900,1000,9000], target = 5 -> -1  (all 8 neighbours of 0000 are jammed)
constraints: All values in deadends are distinct
target may equal 0 (answer 0 if 0 is not a dead end)
hints: Treat every combination as a node of a graph with 10,000 nodes. Which nodes are adjacent to a given one?
Every combination has exactly 8 neighbours (4 wheels times 2 directions). All moves cost the same, so you want the fewest edges from node 0 to the target.

Breadth-first search from 0, never entering a dead end, stopping when the target is reached. Handle the special cases where 0 or the target is a dead end first. A visited array of size 10,000 keeps the search linear.
editorial: The set of combinations forms an unweighted graph where each node has 8 neighbours. A breadth-first search from 0 explores combinations in order of distance, so the first time the target is dequeued or discovered, that distance is the minimum number of moves.

Treat dead ends exactly like visited cells: put them in a set (or mark them in a boolean array) before starting, and never push them. If 0 is a dead end nothing can start, and if the target is a dead end it can never be entered, so both return -1 immediately. A target of 0 needs zero moves.

To extract the digits of a combination use (x // 10**k) % 10; to turn a wheel replace that digit by (d + 1) % 10 or (d + 9) % 10. The graph has at most 10,000 nodes and 80,000 edges, so the search is instantaneous. A bidirectional search would cut the explored area further but is not needed here.
